_readme: Every feature GATE that is OFF unless something turns it on must appear here.
The list of gates is DERIVED by AST (api/services/feature_flag_index.py) and
never typed; tests/test_feature_flag_ledger.py fails BY NAME when a new one
Why this exists: a gate that defaults off and is set nowhere is
indistinguishable, from outside the repo, from a gate that is off ON PURPOSE.
PATTERN_VISION_ENABLED=0 was a deliberate retirement; twelve others measured
on 2026-08-30 were simply never decided. Nothing could tell them apart.
status: armed  = set on at least one Railway service (its value is the decision)
dark   = deliberately off; note MUST say why
pending= built, no decision yet; note + since MUST be present
This file records INTENT. It cannot see Railway, so it can drift from reality:
run tools/flag_ledger_audit.py to compare it against what is actually set.

HISTORY_PREWARM_ENABLED.note: DELIBERATELY OFF, awaiting a NAMED prerequisite -- which is what makes this dark rather than pending. `api/services/history_prewarm.py`'s own module docstring states it: "gated by HISTORY_PREWARM_ENABLED (default OFF -- activate once Cloudflare Tiered Cache + Cache Reserve are on)". ARM IT ONLY AFTER CONFIRMING BOTH ARE ENABLED IN CLOUDFLARE. The sweep walks the whole symbol universe through the public domain to stock the edge; with Cache Reserve OFF that traffic reaches the ORIGIN instead of being absorbed, which is a universe-wide load against the single web pod rather than the cache-filling pass it is meant to be. It runs on the WORKER, off the user request path, and is gentle and sequential so an overlapping pass cannot load the pod -- but that bounds the rate, not the destination. ⚠️ Classified by a passer-by, not its author: the flag arrived in the 'instant-charts Phase 5' commit and tripped test_every_off_by_default_gate_is_declared. Cloudflare's dashboard state is not visible from the repo or from Railway, so the prerequisite could not be checked here -- which is precisely why the answer is 'off with a reason' and not 'on'.

BARS_HISTORY_ORIGIN_ENABLED.note: DELIBERATELY OFF UNTIL A NAMED CUTOVER, which is why this is dark rather than pending. `api/worker_main.py` states it: the worker serves the same edge-cacheable sealed history as the web's `/api/bars-history` but from the worker's deep store, "so Cloudflare can cache deep history worldwide without the web ever holding or fetching the 20 GB (the 2026-08-31 OOM class)", and it is "Gated OFF + lazy-imported (boot path UNCHANGED until cutover)". It is READ-ONLY -- `serve_bars_history` never fetches or writes -- so the risk of arming it is load and routing, not data. Arm it as part of the Phase 5 cutover, with `BARS_HISTORY_PROXY_ENABLED` below, not independently. Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-31-edge-deep-history. ⚠️ Declared by a passer-by, not its author: the flag arrived in the Phase 5 edge-deep-history work and tripped test_every_off_by_default_gate_is_declared. The status reflects what the CODE says about itself, not a decision I am entitled to make.

BARS_HISTORY_PROXY_ENABLED.note: DELIBERATELY OFF UNTIL THE SAME CUTOVER, and it is HALF A SWITCH: `api/routers/bars.py` routes to the worker origin only "when BARS_HISTORY_PROXY_ENABLED=1 AND BARS_HISTORY_ORIGIN_URL is set", so arming this alone changes nothing and arming it without the origin URL is the failure mode to watch for. It is the web-side half of the pair whose worker-side half is `BARS_HISTORY_ORIGIN_ENABLED`; the two are one decision, not two. Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-31-edge-deep-history. ⚠️ Declared by a passer-by, not its author: the flag arrived in the Phase 5 edge-deep-history work and tripped test_every_off_by_default_gate_is_declared. The status reflects what the CODE says about itself, not a decision I am entitled to make.

INSTANT_UNIVERSE_ENABLED.note: PENDING, NOT DARK, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS DELIBERATE. Its two siblings above say WHY they are off -- 'until cutover'. This one's comment in `api/services/bars_prewarm.py` says only "Gated OFF by default; flip INSTANT_UNIVERSE_ENABLED=1 on the worker", which is an instruction for arming it, not a reason it is off. What the surrounding comment DOES explain is the design: the extra D/W/M universe is warmed as a separate boot-only pass rather than folded into `tickers`, so intraday warming stays bound to the active set ("no 26k intraday blow-up") and the 5-minute refresh loop is untouched. That is a rationale for the SHAPE, not for the OFF. DECIDE: arm it on the worker, or mark it dark with the reason it is waiting. ⚠️ Declared by a passer-by, not its author: the flag arrived in the Phase 5 edge-deep-history work and tripped test_every_off_by_default_gate_is_declared. The status reflects what the CODE says about itself, not a decision I am entitled to make.

PERMANENT_DAILY_FRESHNESS_ENABLED.note: DELIBERATELY OFF, and the author said so in two places rather than one: the commit that added it (b6338dce) is titled "after-close full-universe DAILY freshness sweep (dark)", and the block comment in `api/services/bars_prewarm.py` reads "Gated dark by PERMANENT_DAILY_FRESHNESS_ENABLED". That agreement is why this is `dark` and not `pending` -- the intent is recorded, not inferred by me. ⚠️ WHAT IT DOES WHEN ARMED, because the blast radius is the reason it ships off: once per completed session the WORKER re-warms the WHOLE universe's daily bars (ticker_list ∪ _dwm_extra) off-peak, which is a full-universe fetch pass, a bars.db rewrite and a whole-db R2 snapshot. `_scan_stale` + `_boot_can_skip` make day-2 onward near-free (a 1-bar delta), so the cost is concentrated in the FIRST armed run. Buffer hour past the close is PERMANENT_FRESHNESS_HOUR_ET (default 17 = 5pm ET). ⛔ DECLARED BY A THIRD PARTY 2026-09-01: this entry was added by the pattern-library branch because the flag arrived undeclared through a master merge and turned `test_every_off_by_default_gate_is_declared` red. It records the AUTHOR'S stated intent and the code's own behaviour -- nothing about whether it should be armed, which is not this branch's call to make.
